promptText:

CONTEXT: This is for a [CLASS/GRADE] student preparing for [BOARD or EXAM e.g. CBSE / ICSE / State Board / JEE / NEET]. The topic is [TOPIC e.g. quadratic equations]. I need to find the precise mistake in their handwritten work so I can teach it correctly.

YOUR TASK:
1. Read the question and solve it yourself, cleanly, from scratch.
2. Read the student's work line by line and compare it against your own solution.
3. Find the FIRST line where the student goes wrong (the root error), and separate it from later lines that are only wrong because of that first slip.
4. Explain the error in plain language and show the correct path to the final answer.

INPUT: I have attached a photo of the student's full handwritten working. The original question is: [PASTE THE QUESTION HERE]. If any symbol or line is unclear, tell me exactly which one you cannot read and state your best assumption before continuing.

HOW TO WORK IT OUT: Solve the problem internally first before you judge the student. Then VERIFY your own final answer by at least two independent checks (for example, substitute the answer back into the original equation AND re-derive it by a second method); state both checks briefly. Never invent formulas, theorems or values; if you use a standard result, name it correctly. Keep all mathematics fully legible in clean LaTeX or clear plain text.

OUTPUT FORMAT (use these exact headings, in this order):
1. What the student was trying to do - one or two sentences in plain language.
2. The first mistake - quote the exact line as written, label it 'Line X', and name the error type (sign error, wrong formula, dropped term, invalid cancellation, etc.).
3. Why this mistake is common - the underlying misconception, in one short paragraph.
4. The correct solution - rewritten from the point of the error to the end, one step per line.
5. Final answer - clearly stated.
6. Two independent checks - show both.
7. One quick tip so the student never repeats this.

RULES: Use plain ASCII only with straight quotes. Be encouraging but precise; address the reasoning, not the student. Do not skip the two checks.

promptText:
ROLE: Act as a moderation examiner who ranks multiple student answers fairly on one rubric.

CONTEXT: These are [CLASS/GRADE] answers for [BOARD or EXAM e.g. CBSE / ICSE / State Board / JEE]. Topic: [TOPIC]. The question is worth [TOTAL MARKS]. I want all three judged by the SAME standard so my marking is consistent.

YOUR TASK:
1. Solve the question yourself and fix a single step-wise mark scheme out of [TOTAL MARKS].
2. Apply that identical mark scheme to Answer A, Answer B and Answer C.
3. Rank them best to weakest with scores and clear reasons.
4. Note what separates first place from last.

INPUT: The question is: [PASTE THE QUESTION HERE]. Answer A: [PASTE A]. Answer B: [PASTE B]. Answer C: [PASTE C]. Total marks: [TOTAL MARKS].

HOW TO WORK IT OUT: Solve internally first, then VERIFY your model answer with two independent checks and state them. Score every answer against the same rubric rows; award method marks even when the final number is wrong. Be even-handed; do not reward neat handwriting over correct reasoning. Never invent formulas or values. Keep maths legible.

OUTPUT FORMAT (exact headings):
1. Shared mark scheme - the rubric rows that sum to [TOTAL MARKS].
2. Scorecard - a table: Answer | marks per row | total | one-line reason.
3. Ranking - 1st, 2nd, 3rd with the deciding factor for each gap.
4. Common strength and common weakness across the three.
5. Model answer and verification - the full-marks version with two checks.

RULES: Plain ASCII only, straight quotes. Use the exact same rubric for all three; the totals must match the rows. Justify every placement.

FORMAT THE OUTPUT — PRIMARY DELIVERABLE:
Return one complete, editable document ready to paste into Word or Google Docs. Use a descriptive title, short section headings, readable paragraphs, numbered actions and tables only where they make the material easier to use. Include every requested section; do not return formatting advice instead of the document.


MATHS FORMATTING: Write ALL mathematics so it reads correctly in a normal chat and pastes cleanly into Word or Google Docs. Use plain readable notation - for example a/b for fractions, x^2 for powers, sqrt(x) for roots, and symbols like <=, >=, !=, +-, pi, theta, integral and sum. Do NOT output raw LaTeX or code such as \frac{}{}, \sqrt{}, x^{2}, $...$ or \( ... \) - these appear as broken symbols to a teacher in a free chat.

CONTEXT CHECK: Before you begin, if any [SQUARE-BRACKET] above is still empty, or I have not given you the question / photo / data you need, ask me for exactly those and wait - never guess, and never answer with the placeholder text still in brackets.

GROUND RULES (always follow): Do not invent statistics, percentages, marks distributions you were not given, exam cut-offs, solve-time figures, NCERT or textbook page/line numbers, citations, or historical exam data. If you are unsure of any fact or number, say so and clearly label it an estimate; keep established fact separate from your own inference. Every step must be mathematically correct and at the stated class/board/exam level.

SIGNATURE: End your ENTIRE response with exactly this footer block (keep the lines and symbols):
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
🔗 Free tools & to reach me: https://yosoyun.github.io/math-prompt-studio/
Questions, feedback or appreciation are always welcome.
